emergence.summary: A single-pathway disease caused by loss-of-function of either subunit of an obligate heterodimeric amino-acid transporter. SLC3A1 (rBAT, the heavy/chaperone subunit) and SLC7A9 (b0,+AT, the catalytic light subunit) assemble into the rBAT/b0,+AT transporter of the renal proximal-tubule (and intestinal) brush border, which REABSORBS cystine and the dibasic amino acids (ornithine, lysine, arginine) from the lumen -- the BRAKE that keeps filtered cystine from being lost in the urine. Biallelic LOF of EITHER subunit disables the shared transporter (type A = SLC3A1, type B = SLC7A9), so cystine is not reabsorbed and its poorly-soluble free form accumulates in the urine and crystallises into recurrent cystine STONES -> obstructive uropathy and progressive renal damage. The free-urinary-cystine axis is driven UP. Read as a released BRAKE on luminal cystine retention (rBAT/b0,+AT reabsorbs cystine; LOF releases it into the urine -> free urinary cystine UP), and a TWO-CAUSAL-GENE read where both subunits perturb the same axis UP (the HCM / sitosterolaemia convergence pattern -- the THIRD such convergence; the deeper switch, SLC7A9 the catalytic light subunit, is picked as primary). The kit re-derives the established arm -- RESTRAIN the free cystine with a thiol that undergoes thiol-disulfide exchange: tiopronin (and the older D-penicillamine) react with cystine to form a far more soluble cysteine-thiol mixed disulfide, lowering the free-cystine concentration so it no longer crystallises. Urinary alkalinisation (potassium citrate, which raises cystine solubility) and high fluid intake are adjuncts that lower the crystallisation / stone burden. This is the explicit 'CYSTINE, two diseases, two transporters' CONTRAST to cystinosis (CTNS, already in the kit): cystinosis is a LYSOSOMAL cystine-EXPORTER defect -> cystine trapped INSIDE the lysosome (intracellular storage, depleted in situ by the aminothiol cysteamine), whereas cystinuria is a RENAL-TUBULE cystine-REABSORBER defect -> cystine lost into the URINE (luminal stones, solubilised by the thiol tiopronin) -- the SAME molecule, a DIFFERENT transporter, a DIFFERENT compartment, but a strikingly PARALLEL lever (in BOTH a thiol converts cystine into a soluble mixed disulfide; cysteamine intracellularly, tiopronin in the urine). The gamma reads are of the SLC3A1 and SLC7A9 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/splice (e.g. SLC3A1 p.Met467Thr; SLC7A9 p.Gly105Arg), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: free urinary cystine burden (renal-tubular cystine reabsorption / cystine-stone crystallisation) -- the renal-tubular reabsorption contrast to cystinosis's lysosomal cystine-export axis on the same molecule

per_gene.note: SLC7A9 encodes b0,+AT, the CATALYTIC light subunit of the rBAT/b0,+AT brush-border transporter that reabsorbs cystine and dibasic amino acids from the renal proximal tubule -- the functional permease of the heterodimer. Biallelic LOF (cystinuria type B / non-type-I) disables reabsorption -> free cystine is lost into the urine and crystallises (axis UP). 19q13.11 (OMIM 604144). NCBI official symbol SLC7A9. As the catalytic subunit it is the deeper promoter switch of the pair and is picked as primary; the corrective direction is identical for either subunit. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding lesions (e.g. p.Gly105Arg) are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: Feliubadalo 1999 Nat Genet 23:52 (SLC7A9/b0,+AT mutations cause non-type-I cystinuria); Chillaron 2010 Nat Rev Nephrol 6:424 (rBAT/b0,+AT cystine transport)

per_gene.note: SLC3A1 encodes rBAT, the HEAVY/chaperone subunit that traffics the b0,+AT light subunit to the brush-border membrane and is obligatory for transporter assembly; the functional unit is the rBAT/b0,+AT heterodimer, so biallelic LOF of SLC3A1 (cystinuria type A / type I) disables reabsorption just as SLC7A9 loss does -> the same released-brake -> free urinary cystine UP. 2p21 (OMIM 104614). NCBI official symbol SLC3A1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; coding lesions (e.g. the common p.Met467Thr allele) are outside the promoter firewall.
per_gene.src: Calonge 1994 Nat Genet 6:420 (SLC3A1/rBAT mutations cause type-I cystinuria); Palacin 2001 Pflugers Arch 443:S1 (rBAT must heterodimerise with b0,+AT)
